units.text: INT. BARBARA - CONTINUOUS
No malice. So long, Bill.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: SHIRLEY [shaking his head] You make too much of him, miss, in your innocence.
BARBARA [going to him] Peter: I'm like you now.
Cleaned out, and lost my job.
You've youth an hope. That's two better than me. That's hope for you.
units.name: SHIRLEY

units.text: I'll get you a job, Peter, the youth will have to be enough for me.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: She counts her money.
I have just enough left for two teas at Lockharts, a Rowton doss for you, and my tram and bus home.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: He frowns and rises with offended pride.
She takes his arm.
Don't be proud, Peter: it's sharing between friends. And promise me you'll talk to me and not let me cry.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: She draws him towards the gate.
Well, I'm not accustomed to talk to the like of you--
units.name: SHIRLEY

units.text: BARBARA [urgently] Yes, yes: you must talk to me.
Tell me about Tom Paine's books and Bradlaugh's lectures.
Come along.
Ah, if you would only read Tom Paine in the proper spirit, miss!
units.name: SHIRLEY

units.text: They go out through the gate together.
Next day after lunch Lady Britomart is writing in the library in Wilton Crescent.
Sarah is reading in the armchair near the window.
Barbara, in ordinary dresss, pale and brooding, is on the settee.
Charley Lomax enters.
Coming forward between the settee and the writing table, he starts on seeing Barbara fashionably attired and in low spirits.
You've left off your uniform!
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Barbara says nothing; but an expression of pain passes over her face.
LADY BRITOMART [warning him in low tones to be careful] Charles!
LOMAX [much concerned, sitting down sympathetically on the settee beside Barbara] I'm awfully sorry, Barbara.
You know I helped you all I could with the concertina and so forth. [Momentously] Still, I have never shut my eyes to the fact that there is a certain amount of tosh about the Salvation Army.
Now the claims of the Church of England--
That's enough, Charles. Speak of something suited to your mental capacity.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: But surely the Church of England is suited to all our capacities.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: BARBARA [pressing his hand] Thank you for your sympathy, Cholly.
Now go and spoon with Sarah.
LOMAX [rising and going to Sarah] How is my ownest today?
I wish you wouldn't tell Cholly to do things, Barbara. He always comes straight and does them. Cholly: we're going to the works at Perivale St. Andrews this afternoon.
units.name: SARAH

units.text: What works?
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: The cannon works.
units.name: SARAH

units.text: What! Your governor's shop!
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Yes.
units.name: SARAH

units.text: Oh I say!
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Cusins enters in poor condition.
He also starts visibly when he sees Barbara without her uniform.
I expected you this morning, Dolly. Didn't you guess that?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: CUSINS [sitting down beside her] I'm sorry.
I have only just breakfasted.
But we've just finished lunch.
units.name: SARAH

units.text: Have you had one of your bad nights?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: No: I had rather a good night: in fact, one of the most remarkable nights I have ever passed.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: The meeting?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: No: after the meeting.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: You should have gone to bed after the meeting. What were you doing?
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: Drinking.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: }{ Adolphus! SARAH. }{ Dolly! BARBARA. }{ Dolly! LOMAX. }{ Oh I say!
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: What were you drinking, may I ask?
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: A most devilish kind of Spanish burgundy, warranted free from added alcohol: a Temperance burgundy in fact. Its richness in natural alcohol made any addition superfluous.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Are you joking, Dolly?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: CUSINS [patiently] No. I have been making a night of it with the nominal head of this household: that is all.
Andrew made you drunk!
units.name: LADY BRITOMART
